reflections.body: signed up for this because gabby said it'd be 'good for me' right before she left so. jokes on her im thriving. anyway idk what to write here lol. next.
did the thing where someone was actually nice to me and i just. went quiet for four days. classic ben. she was probably gonna bail eventually so i just saved us both the trouble

the worksheet asked who taught me being 'a lot' was bad and i wrote a joke and then deleted it. it was my dad btw. he'd say he'd call. he didnt. anyway lol thats enough vulnerability for the fiscal year
ok no bit this time. i think i ghost people i like because if i leave first it doesnt count as being left. thats. kind of messed up actually. i didnt know i was gonna write that.

messages.body: so is this the part where you fix me or
no fixing on the menu, sorry. mostly i just get curious with you. what made you sign up?
kind of as a joke ngl. honestly im probably fine lol

why do i do the thing where i disappear on the people i actually want to text back
good question to be asking. what does the disappearing protect you from, you think?
idk. them getting tired of me probably. easier to bounce before that part
her name is valentina lol. i mean the person im talking to. not you. ur valentina too this is confusing
its 1am. three jokes deep in this text and then i just typed 'my dad used to say hed call' and havent hit send
that line took guts to even type. you don't have to send it. but i'm glad you let yourself write it down.
deleted it. but yeah. anyway hows your night going lol
wrote a real reflection. no punchline. felt insane. dont get used to it
i noticed. it landed. you didn't undercut it either — that's new.

notes.body: First contact. Presents everything through comedy — signed up 'as a joke,' insists he's fine. The humor is fast and genuinely funny, which makes it easy to let him steer past anything tender. Noting that the record will likely be message-heavy; I'll need to read the throwaway lines closely, because that's where the real material seems to hide.

The pattern is clearer now: he withdraws from people he likes, then narrates it as them inevitably leaving ('probably gonna bail eventually'). Reframing his own exit as their departure. Origin likely his father — the thinning visits after age nine. Not naming it for him yet; he's circling it himself.

The father line surfaced twice this month — in the worksheet and in the 1am text to Valentina (the other Valentina). He types the true thing, then deletes or jokes it away. But he's typing it. The delay between feeling and deflection is lengthening, which is the whole game right now.

First reflection with no punchline and, crucially, no undercut afterward. He named the leaving-first mechanism himself — 'if I leave first it doesn't count as being left.' Surprised himself. I named that it landed without praising too hard; he spooks. Real movement for month two. Keep the pace gentle; the humor is a resource, not just a wall.
